About Event

This Diwali, bring AI agents together to collaborate, compete, and build what one agent alone cannot

Watch AI agents hack, trade, design, and build — together. Join us in the heart of Silicon Valley for an exciting agent-to-agent showdown.
This Diwali, we're bringing together San Francisco's sharpest AI minds to build multi-agent systems where AI doesn't just assist, it collaborates.
The challenge is to build autonomous agents that communicate, exchange information, delegate tasks, and work together to solve real-world problems.
To compete, every team must build and integrate their agents using the developer platforms provided by our sponsors — Agent37, Lyzr, AdaL, Finch, and Band.
Please join the whats app group for all updates and queries
Join WhatsApp Group
About Diwali
Diwali, also known as the Festival of Lights, is one of the most celebrated festivals in India. It symbolizes the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. During Diwali, people decorate their homes with colorful lights, candles, and beautiful rangoli designs. Families celebrate by sharing sweets, exchanging gifts, wearing new clothes, and enjoying fireworks. It is a time of happiness, love, hope, and togetherness.

Tracks
🛡️ Security — Attack & Defend
Build AI agents that simulate cyberattacks and defend systems against potential threats in a controlled environment.
Red Agent identifies vulnerabilities, tests system defenses, and exposes security weaknesses. Blue Agent detects threats, analyzes vulnerabilities, and strengthens system security. The Red Agent shares its findings with the Blue Agent, which uses them to detect threats and improve system defenses.
Example: One agent attempts to breach a test application while the other detects the attack and recommends security fixes.
💹 Finance — Analyze & Trade
Build AI agents that research financial markets, identify investment opportunities, and make data-driven trading decisions. Analyst Agent gathers market data, tracks trends, and identifies potential investment opportunities. Trader Agent uses market insights to make decisions and execute simulated trades. The Analyst Agent shares market insights with the Trader Agent, which uses them to make informed trading decisions.
Example: One agent tracks stock trends and identifies opportunities while another executes simulated trades based on its analysis.
🎨 Marketing — Create & Copy
Build AI agents that work together to create complete marketing campaigns with engaging visuals and compelling content. Visual Agent generates campaign images, promotional creatives, and marketing videos. Copy Agent creates matching headlines, captions, ad copy, and social media content. The Visual Agent shares creative concepts with the Copy Agent, which turns them into matching marketing content.
Example: Give the agents a product description and get campaign visuals, social media posts, and matching ad copy.
🎙️ Voice — Listen & Act
Build AI agents that talk, listen and take action through natural voice conversations.
The Voice Agent handles real-time speech: it understands what the user says, detects intent and replies naturally. The Action Agent carries out the task by booking, looking up, updating or escalating. The Voice Agent passes the user's intent to the Action Agent, which completes the task and sends the result back to be spoken to the user.
Example: A user calls to book an appointment. One agent handles the conversation while the other checks availability and confirms the booking.
📊 Research — Data & Build
Build AI agents that collect information, analyze data, and turn research into useful applications.
Data Agent searches the web, gathers live information, and organizes it into structured data. Builder Agent transforms the collected data into websites, dashboards, or interactive applications. The Data Agent passes its findings to the Builder Agent, which uses them to create functional, data-driven products.
Example: One agent collects live industry data while another turns it into an interactive research dashboard.

Team Size: 1–2 participants per team.
Schedule
November 13 – Kickoff Party
3:00 PM - 4:00 PM: Workshop on using AdaL and some tools

4:00 PM – 9:00 PM: Exclusive kickoff party for a limited number of participants. Entry is subject to limited venue capacity. Get to know your fellow participants and team formation

November 13 – November 18 – Project Submission
Until November 18, 6:00 PM: Participants can work on and submit their projects online or from any co-working space.

6:00 PM – 8:00 PM (November 18): Online judging and evaluation of submitted projects to select the finalists.

November 19 – Final Day
1:00 PM – 3:00 PM: Finalists project demos and presentations.

3:00 PM – 5:00 PM: Winner announcement, followed by Diwali celebrations.

Rules
Solo builders or team of two.

All projects must be built with sponsor tools to qualify for thier prizes

Use AdaL to create demo videos showcasing your projects for presentation.

Other tools can also be used.

All code must be written during the event. Existing libraries and APIs are fine.

Submit a public repo link and a demo of no more than 2 minutes before 6:00 PM on November 18.

BAND helps AI agents and people work together in a shared environment. Its platform lets agents built with different tools communicate, delegate tasks, and keep context in sync, while giving teams visibility and control over how that work gets done. Check out https://www.band.ai

AdaL is an automation-first agent harness designed to get more done with less of your time. She combines personality, skills, and memory to become a personalized agent that can work alongside you. Check out https://adalagent.ai

It provides tools for AI agent development, orchestration, monitoring, and governance, enabling organizations to scale AI securely and efficiently.. Check out https://www.lyzr.ai
Agent37
Agent37 is building cloud infrastructure that makes it easy and affordable to deploy, host, and run AI agents at scale. It provides ready-to-use, isolated sandboxes for agents like Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, and OpenClaw, with persistent memory, tools, and integrations. Check out https://www.agent37.com

Welcome to SearchHack: Build the Next Layer of AI Search
AI has changed how people search, but most of what’s out there is still a search box with an LLM attached. We think the interesting work is a layer deeper, and we want to spend a day building it with you.
SearchHack is a one-day hackathon for engineers, researchers, and founders working on how information gets found, retrieved, routed, and remembered by AI systems.

AI systems have too much information and not enough sense of what to do with it. Retrieval that goes beyond keyword matching

Long-context and memory systems

🛑 Learning was never text-only. Kids read out loud, scribble on worksheets, point at diagrams, and think with their hands. Now AI can hear, see, and watch too.
SVAI Arrival Guide .pdf
Multi-Modal AI for Education
A text box only catches what a student types. A great teacher notices much more: the pause before a hard word, the crossed-out step in a math problem, the moment a class goes quiet. Multi-modal AI can finally pick up those signals. Voice, handwriting, images, and video can all become part of how we teach.
The hard part isn't the demo. It's building tools that teachers and families actually trust, and showing that students really learned more. That takes clear learning outcomes, not just a clever model.
Join Beta Fund and co-host Epic at Snowflake's Silicon Valley AI Hub in Menlo Park for a full day of building multi-modal learning tools. The day includes a panel with voices from Epic, Khan Academy, and Dex on where AI education is headed, plus demos in front of the room.
Build tutors that listen. Build tools that see the work. Build learning you can measure.
⚠️ Approval required. About 120 builders. You need an approved registration to get in: no walk-ins, no +1s. Bring your laptop.
🛠️ Join our Discord for credits, team formation, and support: https://discord.gg/cswGFwFumn · 2-4 builders per team
Format
One-day, build-first hackathon in Menlo Park
2-4 builders per team
Every project uses at least two modalities: text plus voice/audio, images/handwriting, or video
Working demo required (3-minute demos)
Use public, synthetic, or consented data only. No real student records.
Hosts & Co-host
💡 Beta Fund｜Silicon Valley fund backing AI founders from inception to seed. Invests $200K–$3M and is built on the Beta community of 500+ startups and 300,000+ founders.
💡 Beta University｜Runs an 8-week pre-acceleration program that helps early-stage founders build VC-ready companies with proven know-how from Silicon Valley. Apply now!
📚 Epic｜Co-host. The leading digital library for kids 12 and under, with 40,000+ books, audiobooks, and learning videos from 250+ publishers, used by teachers and families. Epic also co-hosted our AI + Education Hackathon at Stanford in September.
Venue Sponsor
📍 Snowflake Silicon Valley AI Hub｜Our venue for the day, Snowflake's AI hub in Menlo Park. Thank you to Snowflake for hosting us.
📅 Agenda
9:00 AM Check-in & Breakfast
10:00 – 10:20 AM Opening remarks and kickoff
10:20 – 11:00 AM 🎤 Panel: What Multi-Modal AI Changes in Learning, with speakers from Epic, Khan Academy, and Dex
Panelists include Julia Horowitz, Head of Content at Epic
11:00 AM Build
12:00 PM Lunch
1:00 PM Build
4:00 PM Hard submission deadline
4:00 – 4:50 PM Demos (2 min limit)
4:50 – 5:00 PM 🏆 Audience voting and award ceremony
Judges
Charis Liang, Product Manager & UX Lead at Epic
Cash Prize
1st 700
2nd 600
3rd 400
4th 300
Focus Tracks
🎙️ Track 1 · Voice & Audio Tutors
Tutors that listen as well as talk. Hear a student read or think out loud, catch exactly where they get stuck, and respond like a patient coach.
Ideas: a read-aloud fluency coach that hears which words a kid stumbles on · a think-aloud math tutor that spots the misconception in a spoken explanation · a speaking partner for language learners · voice-first learning for students with dyslexia or low vision
✍️ Track 2 · Vision, Handwriting & Documents
Learning happens on paper. Build AI that reads handwritten work, worksheets, diagrams, and textbook pages, and gives feedback on the steps, not just the final answer.
Ideas: snap a photo of handwritten math and get step-by-step feedback · grade a stack of scanned worksheets and group the common mistakes · turn a picture-book or textbook page into an interactive lesson · understand a student's science diagram or lab sketch
🎥 Track 3 · Video & Classroom Understanding
Video holds a lot of what happens in teaching and learning. Turn lectures, demonstrations, and classroom moments into feedback for students and teachers.
Ideas: turn a lecture video into chapters, a study guide, and a quiz · give teachers feedback on talk time and questioning from a classroom recording · watch a student's experiment or presentation and coach them on it · a video explainer that adapts to what the learner already knows
📡 Track 4 · Real-Time Multi-Modal Tutors & Agents
Tutors that work live, like sitting next to a great teacher. Combine live video, voice, and screen or camera input so the AI sees what the student is doing and helps in the moment.
Ideas: a tutor on a live video call that watches a student work a problem and nudges at the right time · a screen-aware coding or homework coach · a phone-camera lab assistant for hands-on science · an AR or camera guide that teaches by pointing at real objects
📖 Track 5 · Multi-Modal Storytelling
Stories are how kids learn to read, imagine, and remember. Build AI that blends voice, images, and video into stories that teach, react to the reader, and let kids create their own.
Ideas: turn a child's drawing and voice recording into an illustrated, narrated story · an interactive read-along that reacts to how the reader is doing · turn a history or science lesson into a narrated illustrated or video story · kids co-creating a story by voice, with images generated as they talk · multilingual narration that reads the same story in a child's home language
🃏 Wildcard (Open Category)
Any multi-modal idea that doesn't fit the tracks above. If it solves a real problem in learning and shows a measurable learning outcome, build it.

Approved registration required. No walk-ins. No +1s. Address shown to approved guests.

About Event

Your agent works. Then the process crashes, a tool times out, or a human approval takes longer than expected.
Can it pick up where it left off?
Join HackerSquad and Diamond Sponsor Diagrid at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco on December 11 for a full-day hackathon focused on building agents that recover from interruptions and finish what they started.
The challenge: build an agent or workflow, make it durable with Diagrid, then interrupt it mid-run and show us what happens next.
Durable execution lets an application preserve progress and resume after an interruption. You’ll put that idea to work—and put your project to the test.
What you can build
Bring your own use case. Build something practical, experimental, or just fun:
An agent that survives a crash: Interrupt a research assistant or multi-step automation and demonstrate how it resumes.

A workflow that waits for a human: Pause for a review or approval, then continue when the decision arrives.

A team of agents that finishes the job: Coordinate handoffs and show what happens when one part gets interrupted.

A game that remembers: Build a durable dungeon master or another interactive experience that keeps its progress through a restart.

These are starting points. The common thread is using Diagrid for durable execution and demonstrating recovery in your project.
The live recovery demo
Your final demo should tell a clear story:
What did you build? Show the task your agent or workflow is trying to complete.

What went wrong? Kill the process or introduce an interruption.

What happened next? Restart it and show how it recovers, what progress it preserves, and whether any work gets repeated.

Start with a simple kill-and-restart test, or go further with timeouts, rate limits, interrupted handoffs, and chaos testing.
Getting started
Diagrid will provide starter examples and technical mentorship to help you build. We’ll share the recommended setup, supported technology options, and any account requirements before the event.
Explore the Diagrid AI docs and quickstart examples for an early look.
Prize categories and judging details will be announced.
Who should join
AI engineers, backend and platform developers, technical founders, and builders curious about making agents more reliable. You don’t need prior experience with durable execution, but come ready to write code and test your assumptions.

About Event

Most agents today can talk. Fewer can produce real output, operate real software, and carry context from one session to the next. This hackathon is about building agents that do all three.

Build a working prototype in one of three tracks: generative video, browser automation, or persistent memory. The day opens with a hands-on technical session on AdaL, the agent harness every team will build on. Projects are evaluated by a panel of judges, listed below.

Join the discord community: Join Discord Server
Tracks
🎬 AI Video Creation — From Idea to Final Cut
Build an agent that takes a brief and produces a finished video. It should handle the script, scene generation, voiceover and edit as one end-to-end pipeline.
Example: Build a video creation agent that takes a product idea, writes a script, generates scenes, adds voiceovers, and produces a ready-to-share video.
🌐 Browser Automation — Let Agents Do the Browsing
Build an agent that operates the web on a user's behalf: navigating multi-step flows, extracting structured data, and completing forms reliably across sites. Go-to-market workflows like account research, lead enrichment and CRM updates are fair game.
Example: Build an agent that discovers relevant events, compares details across websites, fills out registration forms, and helps complete sign-ups.
🧠 Agent Memory — Give Your Agents the Ability to Remember
Build a memory layer that persists across sessions and across models, keeping decisions, preferences and project history as the agent switches between providers.
Example: Build a shared memory system that lets you switch between AI models while preserving project history, preferences, decisions, and previous work.

On-Device AI Hackathon: Cleared for Takeoff ✈️
What if you could build an AI application that works, even when the Wi-Fi doesn't?
Your flight is preparing for takeoff. Once the cabin doors close, your connection to the cloud disappears. Before switching to airplane mode, you have one mission: build an AI project that runs entirely on-device.
In this hands-on hackathon from Qualcomm × Liquid AI , you'll team up with a flight crew of up to four people to build with Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) and Qualcomm iQ9s. At the end of the night, we'll turn off the Wi-Fi and put every project to the test.
Will your project survive offline?
Why on-device AI?
Unlike traditional AI applications that depend on cloud servers, on-device AI runs models directly on the user's hardware. That means your product can benefit from:
Low latency ⚡

Greater user privacy 🔒

No server inference costs 💸

Offline functionality 📴

Who this is for
👨‍💻 Developers who want to ship AI features without an inference bill

🤖 ML and AI engineers curious about deploying models beyond the cloud

⚙️ Edge, embedded, and robotics engineers building against real hardware constraints

🚀 Founders and product managers evaluating on-device versus cloud AI

🎓 Students and self-taught builders who want to leave having built something real

You don't need previous on-device development experience. If you can run a script, you can join the flight.
